description: COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, GROUP BY, HAVING — one-row answers from many rows.

questions.explanation: program isn't grouped — SQL can't show one value per program without GROUP BY.
options: program must be in a GROUP BY or be aggregated
AVG can't be used with SELECT
FROM is in the wrong place

questions.prompt: Arrange these lines into a valid query.

questions.code:
SELECT program, COUNT(*)
FROM students
GROUP BY program
___ COUNT(*) > 1;
questions.explanation: HAVING filters groups after they're formed.
questions.prompt: Keep only programs with more than one student.

questions.explanation: Aggregates collapse rows; GROUP BY makes one row per group.
questions.prompt: Match each keyword to its job.

questions.explanation: reduce() builds one object with a key per program, counting as it goes.
questions.prompt: Which JavaScript does the same thing as this SQL?

questions.code:
SELECT program, AVG(gpa)
FROM students
WHERE AVG(gpa) > 3.0
GROUP BY program;
questions.explanation: WHERE filters rows before grouping — it can't see averages. Use HAVING instead.
options: WHERE can't use AVG — aggregates need HAVING
